acceptance: A measurement of scheduled versus expected sweep runs over at least 7 days is recorded
If the gap is real, the docs state the worst-case delay for a lost dispatch, or the sweep gains another trigger, decided with the oracle workstream
context:
Found 2026-10-31 in an adversarial review of oracle queue load; counts came from gh run list. The cause (platform scheduling under load) is an inference. Oracle workflows are soundness paths; any change needs the oracle owner.

Consolidated duplicate item oracle-sweep-schedule-drops-most-runs-20261022 (hourly retry sweep cron drops runs and executes every 2-6 hours).

2026-11-18 observation on PR #4339: the hosted review posted 'reviewers unavailable (provider quota)' for head efaebeea about 03:37Z and stayed pending about 10.5 h, until a manual /review at 14:09Z produced SHIP at 14:19Z. Sweep history: review-verdict scheduled runs fired only at 04:33Z (44238197794) and 14:18Z (cancelled); review-gate only at 10:41Z. The 04:33Z sweep dispatched 5 retries (#4334-#4338) and not #4339: either its retry was not yet due or the sweep caps at 5 (not determined; the logic lives in Theseus review.yml@312ece08). Two causes, then: dropped cron runs (this item) and the sweep skipping a quota-pending head (see review-provider-loss-resilience-20261106).
description: The oracle-gate sweep is the fallback when a dispatch is lost, and it is scheduled hourly (cron '41 * * * *'). On 2026-10-31 only 1 gate schedule run appeared in about 4 hours, and oracle-verdict had 3 schedule runs since 18:44 the previous day. GitHub drops or delays scheduled runs under load, so the fallback cannot be relied on for timing.
